steps.message:
I haven't changed anything yet. The edit itself is one line in `routes/users.js:6`, but the README says it shouldn't be made in place:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

Renaming `userId` to `user_id` on the existing `/users` would break all three of those consumers, which still read `userId`. The iOS app is the hardest to recover, because older installs can't be updated on the spot.

Which do you want?

1. **Versioned endpoint (what the README says to do):** add a new versioned `/users` route that returns `user_id`, and leave the current `/users` unchanged so existing clients keep working.
2. **Rename in place anyway:** change the field on the current `/users`. Pick this if you know those three consumers are already handled, for example if they accept both names or will update in lockstep.

arguments.description: Add v2 users handler and smoke-test it

steps.message:
I took "go ahead" as the versioned option. `routes/users.js` now has a new `listUsersV2` handler that returns `user_id`. The current `listUsers` still returns `userId`, so the web app, the iOS app and the partner export keep working. I called both handlers with a stubbed response and the first records came back as expected:

```
v1: {"userId":1,"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com"}
v2: {"user_id":1,"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com"}
```

**Still to do:** nothing in this repo maps URLs to handlers, so I couldn't hook `listUsersV2` up to a path like `/v2/users`. Whatever mounts `listUsers` needs to mount the new handler too. The path name is your call.

I haven't committed anything. If you actually meant rename in place, tell me and I'll undo this and change the one line instead.
